correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southeastern opening beside Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Primera Sección
correspondence.finding: Both original hydrographic maps depict the selected short northward opening beside Gustavo Díaz Ordaz Primera Sección on the eastern mountain margin. The small channel turns toward the La Arena drainage and visibly connects to the northwestward receiving course. This verifies the chosen opening at ordinary corridor scale; it is not asserted to be the study’s surveyed source of the Pedregal or Tonalá.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Small mapped eastern headwater approach; no independent name assigned to the opening

correspondence.component_scope: La Arena to the Pedregal Moctezuma Segunda Sección approach
correspondence.finding: The mapped drainage continues northwest from the La Arena Segunda Sección area, then through the upper approach east of Los Framboyanes toward Pedregal Moctezuma Segunda Sección. The eastern and western hillside branches are visibly joined to this receiving course. The separate southern mountain drainage and the eastward Grijalva-side watercourses remain outside the selected line; no basin-boundary shortcut is inferred.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Connected eastern approach into the Pedregal corridor; individual feeder names not generalized

correspondence.component_scope: Pedregal Moctezuma to the Río Pedregal settlement corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected northwestward course follows the blue river directly labelled Río Pedregal, passing west of Pedregal Moctezuma Segunda and Primera Sección and continuing past the Río Pedregal settlement. Both the basin map and channel-order map show the connected bends and tributary joins. The selection does not divert onto the separate El Nacimiento–Francisco Villa western feeder or the eastern Río Zanapa branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Nuevo Progreso, lake-rich plain and the Playas connection
correspondence.finding: The river continues west past Nuevo Progreso, through the meandering passage south of the Jicacal and Nanchital lake setting, and joins the northward Playas-side river near the Niños Héroes–Francisco Villa area. The original channel-order map makes this connection visible across the lake-rich plain. The study’s prose identifies the Playas junction as the change from Pedregal to Tancochapa. Nueva and neighbouring lakes are distinguished from the mapped selected channel; a crossing of every adjacent lake is not asserted.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Pedregal into the Tancochapa receiving corridor

correspondence.component_scope: Francisco Villa–Francisco Rueda and the western floodplain turn
correspondence.finding: The selected river proceeds north beside Francisco Villa and Francisco Rueda, then bends west across the mapped flood-prone plain before turning north again. Original map details show the meandering receiving channel continuously through this wetland-rich interval, including side-water connections. La Palma, Tres Zapotes, El Rosario and the other separately drawn waterbodies are contextual waters, not alternative replacements for the selected channel. The route remains geographically connected across the railway and the westward bend.

correspondence.component_scope: Las Choapas, Zanapa junction and first-fragment end
correspondence.finding: The selected northward channel follows the eastern side of Las Choapas and receives the eastward-to-westward Río Zanapa drainage in the surrounding floodplain. The maps depict both the receiving line and its downstream continuation toward El Encanto. The study identifies the Zanapa confluence as the beginning of the Tonalá name. The final part of this fragment remains on that continuous receiving channel; its storage boundary is not treated as a river-name boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Second-fragment start, El Encanto and Blasillo approach
correspondence.finding: The second mainstem fragment resumes on the same mapped channel beyond the first fragment’s endpoint, through the El Encanto vicinity. It continues north through the floodplain toward the Blasillo-side connection and the approach west of La Venta. Río Blasillo enters from the east as a distinct tributary. The continuous original channel depiction supports the fragment join without inferring it from the two stored endpoints alone.

correspondence.component_scope: La Venta, widened lower river and Agua Dulce junction
correspondence.finding: The selected course follows the directly labelled Río Tonalá west of La Venta into its widened lower passage and past the western Agua Dulce junction near Punta Gorda. It remains west of the separate Yucateco lake and canal complex. The infrastructure map and text place Plan Chontalpa drainage works eastward toward Zanapa and navigation canals in the Yucateco floodplain; they do not replace this selected main channel with a managed canal. No through-reservoir segment is depicted on the selected corridor.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Tonalá lower river and estuarine approach

correspondence.component_scope: Chicozapote-side connection and actual Tonalá coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The original maps show the widened river continuing past the Chicozapote-side connection to the coastal opening at Tonalá, beside the Cuauhtemoczin setting identified in the study’s outlet photograph. The selected final parts reach this same river-mouth corridor. The connected blue river and Gulf body, together with the original outlet description and photograph, establish the actual coastal terminal independently of the modeled sea flag. The adjacent Tortuguero–El Gavilán outlet is a different drainage.
correspondence.named_reach_scope: Río Tonalá outlet to the Golfo de México

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and westward headward connector
correspondence.finding: The initial selected northward opening is only partly represented. A mapped elongated waterbody and northern bend correspond to some opening portions, but the selected westward continuation into the Duncan setting crosses broad blank areas between mapped waters. Nearby waterbodies and the model connection do not establish the missing stream or wetland links.

correspondence.component_scope: Entry into and crossing of Lac Duncan
correspondence.finding: Following the unresolved headward connector, the selected line enters the eastern lake setting and crosses the waterbody labeled Lac Duncan toward its western end. The original depicts the lake passage and the next southward connection at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Duncan–Esprit connection and southern outlet setting
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the southward connection from the western Duncan lake end to the elongated waterbody labeled Lac Esprit, followed by the southern outlet corridor and its junction with the westward lower watercourse. These connected passages correspond to the selected south-and-west turn.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle westward course and lower northwestern bend
correspondence.finding: The mapped watercourse continues west from the Esprit outlet setting, passes the southern joining corridor and turns northwest toward the lower Comb reach. The successive bends and joining settings correspond to the selected middle and lower parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower branching corridor and actual northern coastward ending
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the selected lower branch turning north and then west into the James Bay coast and distinguishes this northern approach from an adjacent more southerly outlet. The Rivière Comb label lies by the neighboring lower branching setting; label proximity alone does not determine the name of the selected northern terminal branch. A thick territorial-boundary symbol obscures immediate shoreline detail, but does not leave a separate inland through-link gap at ordinary coastal-corridor scale. No exact mouth vertex, bank or tidal boundary is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern opening and off-sheet initial feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and the initial northward approach lie west of the inspected Overby sheet. The map first becomes useful farther along the selected feeder. Neither the selected opening's waterbody nor its complete connection to that mapped portion is established by the inspected sources.

correspondence.component_scope: On-sheet southern feeder and narrow lake passages
correspondence.finding: Along the western edge of the Overby sheet, the selected northward approach follows a mapped chain of narrow unnamed waterbodies and connecting stream reaches. The elongated southern lake passage, intervening smaller widenings and curved northern stream can be followed at ordinary corridor scale. The larger basin labeled Overby Lake is east of this selected approach and is not traversed by it.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern receiving-river join and short westward named reach
correspondence.finding: The selected southern feeder reaches the river printed Hiukitak R. near the western map margin. The map shows the join, adjacent river widening and westward continuation to the sheet edge. The name applies to the mapped receiving reach; the feeder and its small lakes are not thereby assigned one uniform river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Off-sheet middle continuation, westward reach and northern bend
correspondence.finding: After the mapped reach leaves the Overby sheet, the selected route continues through a substantial westward inland reach and turns north. No inspected permitted map establishes the complete sequence, its intervening joins or any lake and wetland passages. The nearby printed hydronym and broad coastal destination are insufficient to bridge this material gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: CHS ARC403 Chapter6 places the mouth of Hiukitak River south-southeast of Fowler Bay and describes its entry into Bathurst Inlet through a steep-sided valley. This is useful receiving-water and coastal context. It does not map the final selected westward reach or distinguish the stored rendered terminal from the modeled source sea point, so actual terminal correspondence remains unfinished.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Bathurst Inlet, contextual receiving water only

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and eastward traverse north of La Vega
correspondence.finding: The municipal plan identifies Río Verde as tributary of Río Licey and locates Río Verde Arriba/Cutupú relative to Licey. The municipal boundary map and urban-risk map do not expose the entire selected opening and eastward reach. The watershed network map is too sparsely labelled here to choose among the depicted tributaries. No name is assigned to this opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward connector from the northern approach into the Camú plain
correspondence.finding: Licey is explicitly a Camú tributary in the municipal plan, but the acquired cartography does not independently tie this selected southward connector and its join to Licey. The connection is retained as a required material gap rather than being filled from network hierarchy alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeast-running lower Camú corridor in the La Vega agricultural plain
correspondence.finding: The municipal description places the Camú through the La Vega plain toward Yuna. The project watershed map depicts the matching southeast-running lowland trunk continuing toward the labelled Camú en La Bija station. This supports lower-Camú corridor identity, but does not retroactively identify the unresolved northern feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Camú, La Bija area and confluence transition near Hostos
correspondence.finding: The watershed map marks Camú en La Bija on the western inflow and shows its connection into the eastward lower trunk. Tobey identifies the Camú–Yuna confluence near Hostos and says Yuna continues east across the lower plain. The selected approach and join agree at corridor scale. The precise part or vertex at which the river name changes is not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward lower Yuna plain after the Camú confluence
correspondence.finding: The inspected network map connects the confluence to the lower Yuna eastward trunk and its southward floodplain excursion. Tobey describes the downstream Cevicos, Payabo and Guaraguao tributary setting. The selected mainstem follows that lower river corridor; no tributary name is extended over the mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower-Yuna northward excursion and return through the Villa Riva–El Limón corridor
correspondence.finding: The watershed map depicts the connected lower-Yuna route through the Villa Riva and El Limón station setting. Tobey places these stations on the lower Yuna and identifies El Limón upstream of the Agua Santa split. The selected bends and connections agree at ordinary regional scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward irrigated floodplain toward Agua Santa and the estuarine bifurcation setting
correspondence.finding: The project sources depict and describe a continuous lower Yuna entering the wetland margin after El Limón. Rice irrigation, diversion works and the eventual Barracote connection form part of this setting. The selected eastward channel is not relabelled as an irrigation canal. The source material does not establish current gate operations or current distribution of flow, which are outside this naming finding.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastward wetland passage, final eastward reach and actual Bahía de Samaná outlet near Sánchez
correspondence.finding: Herrera-Moreno Figure 7 shows the Yuna meandering northeast through freshwater marsh and mangrove to the northern outlet, separately from Barracote farther south. Its Annex II bathymetric map labels Río Yuna at the western bay shore south of Sánchez, with Barracote a distinct southern mouth. Those inspected maps and Tobey’s old-outlet explanation support the selected terminal at ordinary estuary scale. This does not assert a present natural/unmodified flow regime, exact tidal boundary or modern bank position.
